title: Senior Backend Engineer (Multiple Positions)
description:
Remote - US

About LaunchDarkly Engineering

LaunchDarkly helps engineering organizations ship software and AI with speed, safety, and control. Our platform gives teams the confidence to release gradually, target experiences to the right audiences, learn through experimentation, understand what is happening in production, and respond quickly when risk appears.

Our engineers build the systems, services, SDKs, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, and product experiences that make this possible. The work spans high-scale distributed systems, reliable data and event pipelines, intuitive enterprise workflows, and AI-powered capabilities that help teams manage the next generation of software delivery.

LaunchDarkly’s SDKs are used in systems that perform trillions of feature flag evaluations each day, giving our engineering work a direct connection to the reliability and customer experience of software around the world. As the company grows, we are expanding beyond traditional feature management into experimentation, observability, and AgentControl—helping customers control more of the software and AI lifecycle. That creates an unusually broad set of technical challenges, visible customer impact, and room for engineers to shape what comes next.

We believe in the power of teams. We work with humility, openness, curiosity, and care; we value clear communication, thoughtful technical judgment, inclusive collaboration, and a strong sense of ownership. We encourage people to apply even when they do not meet every qualification listed below. We are interested in the experience, perspective, and potential you would bring to the role.

About the role

We have multiple backend engineering roles open on various teams. The specific level, scope, and technical focus will be aligned to the opportunity and the candidate’s experience. Experience with cloud platforms, distributed systems, developer tools, SDK engineering, data infrastructure, observability, or AI/agent systems may be relevant for some teams.

Candidates may be considered for opportunities across product engineering, core engineering, feature management, observability, experimentation, data platform, cloud infrastructure, SDKs, and AI/agent product areas, depending on experience, interests, and business need.

As a Senior Backend Engineer at LaunchDarkly, you will design, build, and operate the services that power reliable software delivery for our customers. You may work on APIs, distributed systems, configuration and event pipelines, data services, SDK-related infrastructure, platform capabilities, or backend systems supporting our product experiences.

You will take ownership of complex, high-impact work from problem definition through production and iteration. You will partner with Product, Design, Staff Engineers, Engineering Managers, and adjacent teams to turn customer and business needs into simple, scalable solutions. Your work will influence technical direction within your team and, where appropriate, across team boundaries.

What you’ll do

  • Lead the design and delivery of large or ambiguous backend projects, breaking them into clear milestones and creating alignment with partners.
  • Design, implement, test, and operate production services and APIs that are scalable, secure, observable, and maintainable.
  • Make and communicate thoughtful tradeoffs across scalability, performance, reliability, security, maintainability, cost, and delivery speed.
  • Identify architectural risks, performance bottlenecks, operational gaps, and sources of technical friction; then drive durable improvements.
  • Improve the observability and operability of the systems you own, including metrics, logs, traces, alerting, service-level objectives, and incident follow-through.
  • Collaborate with Product, Design, Support, Customer Success, and other engineering teams to understand needs and deliver measurable customer outcomes.
  • Influence technical direction through design documents, architecture discussions, code reviews, and clear written and verbal communication.
  • Mentor engineers, raise the quality of technical decision-making, and contribute to a culture of inclusive collaboration and continuous improvement.
  • Participate in production support and incident response with calm ownership, turning operational lessons into lasting improvements.
  • Help evolve engineering practices, reusable patterns, and developer experiences that make other teams more effective.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience building and operating production software, with a track record of delivering meaningful customer or business impact.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, testing, debugging, API design, and distributed-systems concepts.
  • Deep experience with a backend language such as Go, Python, Rust, or an equivalent language. (Most of our teams use Go)
  • Experience designing systems that must remain reliable, observable, secure, and maintainable as usage, complexity, and team ownership grow.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects with ambiguous requirements, multiple stakeholders, or cross-team dependencies.
  • Sound judgment when evaluating architecture, technology choices, operational risk, and short- versus long-term tradeoffs.
  • Ability to explain complex technical decisions clearly and build alignment with technical and non-technical partners.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and strengthening team practices through feedback, documentation, pairing, or technical leadership.
  • A strong sense of ownership for production outcomes and downstream customer impact.
  • Comfort learning unfamiliar systems and navigating changing priorities with curiosity and a collaborative mindset.

Pay:

Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level 4:

  • Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $191,800 - $263,670**
  • Zone 2:Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $172,600 - $237,270*
  • Zone 3: All other US locations - $ 163,000 - $224,070 **

LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

*Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas.

** Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), health, vision, and dental insurance, and mental health benefits in addition to salary.

About LaunchDarkly:

Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations.

The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

  • Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages
  • Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts
  • Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize
  • Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types
  • Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights into engineering cadence and stability

title: Specialist, Political & External Affairs
description:
The American Academy of Dermatology is seeking a Specialist, Political & External Affairs located in our Washington, DC. office responsible for providing project coordination for the Advocacy and Policy department political and external affairs; provide public policy engagement, research, and analytic support. Support day-to-day operations of AADA’s political action committee (SkinPAC). Assists with grassroots advocacy programs. Collects, compiles, assembles and distributes materials for committee meetings. Works closely with our sister societies, state societies and various patient and disease coalitions.

About Us:

The American Academy of Dermatology (Academy), founded in 1938, is the largest, most influential, and most representative of all dermatologic associations. A sister organization to the Academy, the American Academy of Dermatology Association is the resource for government affairs, health policy and practice information for dermatologists, and plays a major role in formulating policies that can enhance the quality of dermatologic care.


With a membership of more than 21,000 members worldwide, the Academy is committed to: advancing the diagnosis and medical, surgical, and cosmetic treatment of the skin, hair, and nails; advocating high standards in clinical practice, education, and research in dermatology; and supporting and enhancing patient care for a lifetime of healthier skin.


To learn more about the Academy please visit our website at , or follow us on these social media outlets:

  • Facebook ()
  • TikTok (www.tiktok.com/@AADskin)
  • Pinterest ()
  • Instagram ()


Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate projects including maintaining member databases and spreadsheets, identifying and planning critical tasks, preparing project timelines, and monitoring progress of projects. Work with staff to coordinate council, committee and staff meeting logistics and agenda materials for Councils, Committees, and Task Forces as needed.


  • Coordinate all projects related to our coalition partners. Including coordinating meetings and conference calls, drafting correspondence, preparing agendas and summation reports, and other duties as needed.


  • Maintain SkinPAC database, website and fundraising tools. Manage disbursement requests and coordinate participation in political events.


  • Work with Advocacy & Policy staff to keep grassroots database current and disseminate advocacy alerts.


  • Monitor, track, research and analyze information on patient and member coalition relevant to dermatology.


  • Coordinate and compile background research, data collection, and analysis on health care policy issues as needed. Assist with report writing as needed.


  • Composes and prepares draft correspondence, reports and presentation materials for committee meetings.


  • Research & respond to inquiries and requests from Academy members and the general public via email and phone. Use judgment to determine those that require priority attention.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required.
  • Experience working with database management software.
  • Minimum two years’ experience, working or interning on Capitol Hill, on a campaign, for a law firm or in an association, providing project coordination, member management, and/or event planning.
  • Association experience preferred.
  • A strong desire to learn on the job about direct advocacy and practical politics.
  • Interest in the healthcare field and medical advocacy.
  • Collaboration – Establishes and maintains effective work relationships, works cooperatively in group situations. Offers assistance and support to coworkers.
  • Communication – Apply effective verbal, nonverbal, and written communication methods to achieve desired results. Respond intelligently to standard business correspondence. Demonstrate sufficient business vocabulary to communicate effectively.
  • Decision Making – Able to exercise discretion and independent judgment to understand issues, identify problems and opportunities to determine the appropriate course of action. Demonstrate sound decision-making skills with an increasing number of alternatives to be reviewed by management.
  • Dependability – Able to follow through on assignments and instructions in a reliable, trustworthy and timely manner. Responds productively to requests for service and assistance.
  • Goal Implementation – Ensure goals are converted into actions; obtain results despite conflicting priorities, lack of resources, or ambiguity.
  • Integrity – Demonstrate personal integrity in all interactions. Ability to maintain confidentiality.
  • Organization – Able to organize, prioritize, and coordinate multiple tasks and timelines. Monitor the progress of tasks and projects.


We offer a competitive compensation plan and benefits package including medical/dental/vision/life insurance as well as a matching retirement contribution, tuition reimbursement, bonus program, pension plan, paid vacation/medical/personal days, work-life balance, recognition program and casual work environment. More information about our compensation and benefits can be reviewed on the detailed job ad on our website.


The Academy offers a hybrid work environment; providing time in the office for in-person collaboration and the opportunity to work remotely for focus time. We are building a workplace where our employees are excited to come to work every day because of the culture that we are creating together — one of respect, transparency, and collaboration. A workplace in which we demonstrate care and commitment, celebration, community, and focused learning that contributes to the mission of advancing excellence in dermatologic care.

title: Sr Software Engineer - SAP Commerce Cloud
description:
Job Description

Job Description We are seeking a highly skilled Senior SAP Commerce Cloud Developer to design, develop, and maintain our enterprise-grade digital commerce platform. As a core development team member, you will build robust and scalable eCommerce features using SAP Commerce Cloud (Hybris), lead technical problem‑solving, and support integration with SAP and third‑party systems. This is a hands‑on role ideal for someone who is passionate about delivering best‑in‑class customer experiences in a fast‑paced, agile environment.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Develop and maintain custom modules and extensions in SAP Commerce Cloud using Java and Spring Framework.
  • Participate in full software development lifecycle, including design, implementation, testing, and deployment.
  • Design scalable and reusable components aligned with best practices and enterprise architecture.
  • Own core eCommerce functionality (catalog, pricing, cart, checkout, order management).
  • Customize B2B and/or B2C accelerators as needed.
  • Integrate SAP Commerce Cloud with backend systems (e.g., SAP ERP, S/4HANA, SAP CPI, payment gateways, PIM, OMS).
  • Design APIs and data flows for real‑time and batch interfaces.
  • Conduct code reviews and enforce high standards for performance, security, and maintainability.
  • Write unit, integration, and performance tests to ensure code reliability.
  • Work closely with product managers, QA engineers, UX designers, and DevOps teams in an Agile/Scrum setup.
  • Participate in grooming, sprint planning, and retrospective meetings.
  • Investigate and resolve production issues, system bottlenecks, and performance challenges.
  • Perform root cause analysis and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives.
PREFERRED EDUCATION
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field.
  • 5+ years of professional experience in Java development, with 3+ years in SAP Commerce Cloud (Hybris) development.
  • Strong understanding of SAP Commerce architecture, data modeling, and extension mechanisms.
  • Experience with B2B/B2C Accelerators and OCC (OmniCommerce Connect) APIs.
  • Proficiency in Spring Framework, RESTful services, and SOLR.
  • Familiarity with cloud deployments (e.g., SAP Commerce Cloud in public cloud environments) and CI/CD tools.
  • Working knowledge of SAP integrations and commerce‑specific tools (e.g., SmartEdit, Backoffice, Impex).
Preferred Qualifications
  • SAP Certified Development Specialist – SAP Commerce Cloud.
  • Experience with headless commerce and frontend technologies like Spartacus or React.
  • Knowledge of performance tuning and caching strategies (e.g., Redis, CDN).
  • Experience in Agile and DevOps environments.
  • Understanding of GDPR, PCI‑DSS, or other compliance standards relevant to e‑commerce.
PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS

Typically, to advance to a new job level, a candidate must demonstrate professional behaviour and should consistently be at the high end of meeting expectations or consistently exceed expectations.

TRAVEL / PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Travel typically less than 10%. Office environment. No special physical demands required.

title: Director of Revenue Cycle
description:
Bradford Health Services provides addiction treatment programs, resources, and community for every aspect of recovery. Through our premier drug and alcohol rehab facilities across the Southeast, we provide affordable, evidence-based addiction treatment with proven outcomes at every level of care. We’re guided by unity and dedicated to meeting and treating every patient right where they are. Bradford is more than a healthcare network; we are recovery communities for every stage of the journey.

We are seeking a Director of Revenue Cycle to add to our dynamic team. The Director of Revenue Cycle Operations leads the daily operations and ongoing transformation of billing, accounts receivable, payment posting, cash reconciliation, credit balance, and related revenue cycle functions across a complex, multi-state behavioral healthcare organization. Reporting to the Vice President of Revenue Cycle, the Director is accountable for timely and accurate claim submission, effective payer follow-up, accurate payment and adjustment posting, disciplined account resolution, and measurable improvement in cash, aging, quality, and productivity.

This is a hands-on operational leadership role. The Director must understand the detailed mechanics of claims, work queues, clearinghouse transactions, payer edits, remittances, denials, adjustments, unapplied cash, refunds, and account documentation. The leader will personally analyze workflows and representative accounts when needed, establish standardized processes and desk-level procedures, design an effective organizational structure, identify system limitations and configuration opportunities, and evaluate responsible uses of automation and artificial intelligence. The role partners with Centralized Admissions Department, Patient Financial Services, Utilization Review, Clinical Operations, Finance, Information Technology, Compliance, and external vendors while maintaining clear ownership of back-end revenue cycle execution.


Responsibilities

  • Provide direct operational leadership for billing, accounts receivable follow-up, payment posting, cash reconciliation, credit balances, refunds, and related back-end revenue cycle functions
  • Maintain detailed knowledge of daily inventory, work queues, claim status, billing holds, clearinghouse rejections, payer responses, payment exceptions, aged accounts, and unresolved operational barriers
  • Conduct detailed reviews of workflows and representative patient accounts to determine what occurred, what should have occurred, and what corrective action is required
  • Design and standardize end-to-end workflows from charge release and claim creation through payment, follow-up, adjustment, refund, and final account resolution
  • Establish clear ownership, handoffs, service-level expectations, escalation pathways, and quality controls for every major billing, accounts receivable, and payment-posting workflow
  • Oversee claim generation, claim-edit resolution, clearinghouse submission, payer acceptance, rejection correction, and timely filing controls
  • Develop payer-specific accounts receivable strategies using age, balance, payer, denial reason, filing limit, reimbursement risk, and probability of collection to prioritize work
  • Establish standards for follow-up frequency, account documentation, next-action dates, escalation, appeal, write-off review, and final disposition
  • Oversee accurate ERA and manual payment posting, contractual and non-contractual adjustments, denial posting, recoupments, takebacks, unapplied cash, deposits, refunds, and daily and monthly reconciliation
  • Create controls that ensure posted cash and adjustments reconcile to bank deposits, remittance files, general ledger activity, and expected payer reimbursement
  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, desk-level instructions, workflow maps, training materials, audit tools, and change-control processes
  • Establish daily, weekly, and monthly productivity, quality, timeliness, and inventory standards by function and role
  • Build dashboards and operating reviews that translate revenue cycle data into clear actions, owners, deadlines, and measurable outcomes
  • Design the billing, accounts receivable, and payment operation’s organizational structure based on actual workload, transaction volumes, skill requirements, span of control, and future growth
  • Assess staffing needs, role clarity, management layers, workload distribution, cross-training, coverage plans, and opportunities to consolidate or specialize work
  • Develop leaders and front-line team members through clear expectations, coaching, training, quality feedback, performance management, and succession planning
  • Identify process failures, system limitations, configuration issues, interface gaps, duplicate work, and manual workarounds that create delay, error, or unnecessary cost
  • Partner with Information Technology, system vendors, and operational stakeholders to define requirements, test changes, validate outcomes, and sustain improvements
  • Evaluate automation and artificial intelligence opportunities using clear business cases, expected return, workflow impact, data quality, privacy, compliance, and human oversight requirements
  • Prioritize process correction and standardization before automating unstable or poorly controlled workflows
  • Lead backlog reduction, system remediation, payer-specific improvement initiatives, and other focused recovery efforts while protecting current production
  • Partner with Patient Access and Utilization Review leaders to resolve upstream issues affecting claim quality or reimbursement without assuming operational ownership of those functions
  • Collaborate with Finance on cash reporting, month-end close, reserves, write-offs, refunds, reconciliation, and financial reporting accuracy
  • Maintain compliance with HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, payer contracts, governmental requirements, internal controls, and organizational policies
  • Perform other duties assigned in support of Revenue Cycle and organizational objectives.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business, finance, accounting, health information management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant leadership experience
  • Minimum 10 years of progressive healthcare revenue cycle experience, including at least 5 years leading billing, accounts receivable, payment posting, or closely related back-end revenue cycle operations
  • Demonstrated expert-level knowledge of the day-to-day mechanics of claim generation and submission, claim edits and rejections, payer follow-up, denial resolution, remittance processing, contractual adjustments, cash reconciliation, credit balances, refunds, and final account resolution
  • Demonstrated experience personally reviewing claims, work queues, remittances, account notes, system transactions, and workflow exceptions to identify root causes and verify operational performance
  • Demonstrated experience building, centralizing, restructuring, or materially improving healthcare billing, accounts receivable, or payment operations
  • Experience developing standard operating procedures, desk-level workflows, role definitions, productivity expectations, quality audits, performance dashboards, and escalation pathways
  • Experience designing staffing models and organizational structures using inventory, transaction volumes, payer mix, complexity, service-level expectations, and productivity assumptions
  • Experience identifying system limitations, configuration gaps, manual workarounds, and opportunities for workflow automation
  • Strong analytical ability with experience using revenue cycle data to diagnose operational problems and drive corrective action
  • Proven ability to lead managers and front-line teams through change while maintaining daily production, quality, accountability, and staff engagement
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, payer requirements, and applicable federal and state billing and collection requirements


Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in healthcare administration, business administration, finance, or a related field
  • Behavioral health and substance use disorder revenue cycle experience, including residential, inpatient, partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient, and outpatient services
  • Experience within a multi-site and multi-state healthcare organization with centralized revenue cycle operations
  • Experience with commercial insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, Managed Medicaid, TRICARE, Veterans Affairs, and other government or managed-care payers
  • Experience optimizing an electronic health record, practice management system, clearinghouse, payer portal, banking platform, or revenue cycle work queue solution
  • Experience evaluating or implementing automation, robotic process automation, machine learning, or artificial intelligence solutions within revenue cycle operations
  • Experience with system conversions, mergers, acquisitions, integrations, or rapid organizational growth
  • Professional certification such as CHFP, CRCR, HFMA certification, or an equivalent revenue cycle credential

description:
Job Summary – Scanning Coordinator


Essential Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Approximately 13 - 29 hours per week assisting the Scanning Coordinator with various responsibilities, including but not limited to, assisting with bi-weekly ad changes, hanging tags, creating and printing tag batches and the ability to learn and use the signage program.
  • Provide prompt and courteous service to the customers according to company policies which promote the McCaffrey’s brand
  • Requires some basic computer knowledge with the ability to learn the necessary tag/sign program
  • Operate scanning computer equipment to ensure accurate prices and codes for all store products.

  • Verify print and on-line information for advertising purposes.

  • Perform other functions as requested or required by business needs.

  • Maneuver in a vertical range from floor to seven feet in order to change shelf tags.
  • Work in front of a computer in a semi-confined environment for long periods of time.
  • Requires daytime availability
  • Lift, push, and/or pull items up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to wear company-provided uniform, and maintain a clean and groomed appearance.


Skills Requirements:

  • Friendly personality and “customer service” mentality.
  • Good mathematic skills to operate scales & computers and to coordinate dates for inventory rotation.

title: Railcar Repair Technician
description:
Build Your Career With a Team That Keeps America Moving

Cypress Rail Solutions is hiring Railcar Repair Technicians to support railcar inspection, maintenance, and repair operations in the field. This role is part of our Richardton Team and offers hands‑on work, variety in job locations, and the opportunity to grow your skills alongside experienced rail professionals.


Whether you’re building your railcar repair experience or bringing a strong mechanical background to the field, this is a chance to work with a stable company that values safety, skill, and teamwork.

What You’ll Do

  • Perform mobile railcar repairs under the guidance of a lead or Level 2 technician
  • Remove and replace brake systems, couplers, draft gears, air hoses, valves, and fittings
  • Repair or replace structural components including side posts, floors, panels, piping, and underframes
  • Weld, burn, straighten, patch, and install steel components using proper tools and procedures
  • Stencil letters and numbers and prepare railcars for painting
  • Inspect, clean, and maintain railcar surfaces and components
  • Safely move, position, and handle heavy equipment and railcar parts
  • Assist with switching, ground operations, and track mobile equipment as trained
  • Follow all safety rules, FRA, AAR, and company procedures

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong mechanical aptitude and hands‑on repair skills
  • Welding and machine experience preferred
  • Ability to read and follow safety rules, work instructions, and procedures
  • Willingness to learn rail industry rules and regulations
  • Reliable, safety‑focused, and able to work independently or as part of a team
  • Comfortable working outdoors, on uneven surfaces, and in varying weather conditions
  • Able to travel daily (50%+) and work flexible hours as job demands change
  • Railcar repair experience is a plus but not required—training will be provided for qualified candidates
  • CDL preferred

Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • Full‑time, stable employment
  • Mobile work that offers variety and field experience
  • On‑the‑job training and skill development
  • Supportive leadership and team‑driven culture
  • Competitive pay based on experience and comprehensive benefits

Join a company where your work matters, your skills are valued, and your effort helps keep rail freight moving safely across the country.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities but are not limited to:

  • Stencil letters and numbers on cars.
  • Fasten parts of car using impact wrench or hydraulic bolt fastener for riveting.
  • Remove and replace brake assemblies and brake shoes.
  • Remove and replace uncoupling lever.
  • Repair or replace steel sections such as side posts, rafters, crossties, panels, under framing, and piping using welding torch, electric welder, power wrench, and hand tools.
  • Replace and/or repair gaskets, air hose, train line, etc., as required.
  • Straighten and/or replace grab irons, handholds, still steps on cars.
  • Maintain, repair, or replace air brake pipes, valves, fitting, or other appurtenances.
  • Remove and replace couplers, draft gears, and yokes.
  • Clean and prepare surfaces of railroad cars or cabooses to be painted.
  • Repair freight car sides, ends, doors and floors by burning, straightening, or patching.
  • Pull, push, and position heavy equipment or car components when making or completing repairs.
  • Other duties as assigned by foreman/manager.
  • Ability to throw/align a switch.
  • Ability to be trained as track mobile operator and/or groundman.

Competencies:

To perform this job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies:

  • Good mechanical background will be required to become conversant with the General Code of Operating Rules, Safety Rules, AAR Rules and regulations, and FRA requirements.
  • Welding and machine experience preferred.
  • Apply principles of rational systems to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of variables in situations where only limited standardization exists.
  • Be able to read and understand safety rules, instructions in the use and maintenance of shop tools and equipment, and methods and procedures in mechanical drawing and layout work.


Physical Demands:

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the physical demands listed below:

  • The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to perform on uneven or slippery surfaces, platforms, ladders, equipment in all weather and temperature conditions. Most of the day could be spent on feet standing. Eye/hand coordination, hand/feet dexterity and grasping hand tools, materials & equipment is required. The employee is frequently required to perform manual labor & physical activities that require considerable use of the whole body, such as standing and lifting from various levels.
  • Additional physical demands are listed in the chart below.

Environmental:

  • Continuous: Standing on concrete.
  • Occasional: Vibration, noise, hot or cold temperature extremes, work at heights, uneven surfaces, shift work, paperwork, travel, smoke & dust, paint, cramped quarters & moving machinery.
  • Wash rail cars outside in all weather conditions.
  • Must wear correct PPE and masks for identified jobs and painting.


Education and Training:

  • GED or higher.
  • Must have and maintain an insurable driving status which includes but is not limited to CRS driver provisions.

Requirements of Joining Our Team:

Our comprehensive pre-employment process ensures the well-being and integrity of our team. To join our organization, candidates are required to:

1.  Pass a mandatory drug test to maintain a drug-free workplace. Random, reasonable suspicion and post-accident testing may also be required throughout employment.

    2.    Undergo a thorough physical examination to ensure the requirements of the position can be met.

    3.    Provide professional references to validate qualifications and character.

    4.    Complete a comprehensive background check to confirm suitability for the position.

This job description is not intended to represent a complete, comprehensive list of all duties and responsibilities that may be required in this position. There may be unplanned activities and other duties assigned. This Job Description may change at any time declared by Management.

Cypress Rail Solutions is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race,

color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran, or any other

characteristic protected under local, state, or federal statute, ordinance, or regulation.

description:
Job Title

Cross-Functional Partners

National Team, Communications Team

Position Status

Temporary

Purpose of the Triage Desk:

From mid-October through the week following Election Day, the Triage Desk will provide additional capacity to All Voting is Local's state teams during the highest-volume portion of the election cycle. This is a temporary role that will last for one month: October 13 - November 13, 2026.

The Desk exists to help identify, organize, route, and track emerging needs so State Directors can remain focused on executing their state strategies.

Requirements:

  • Participate in virtual boiler room operations between October 13 - October 30 and November 8 - November 13.
  • Attend and participate in an in-person boiler room in Washington, D.C., starting on Sunday, 11/1 and ending on Saturday, 11/7.
    • For candidates who are not local to D.C., travel and accommodations will be covered by All Voting.
Compensation:
  • $2,200 per week from October 13 - October 30 and November 8 - November 13 (virtual boiler room)
  • $3,200 for the week of November 1-7 (in-person boiler room)

Core Responsibilities:

The Triage Desk is not a parallel strategy team and does not replace the judgment or decision-making authority of State Directors. Consultants should approach this role first as listeners and problem-solvers: understand what is happening, determine what support is needed, and help connect the right people and resources.
  1. Monitor and identify emerging needs by staying in regular communication with assigned states and maintain awareness of emerging election administration issues, threats, partner needs, and opportunities.
    1. The goal is not simply to collect information, but to identify: What is happening? Does it require action? Who needs to know? What support does the state need?
    2. Help distinguish between:
      1. Issues the state team can handle directly;
      2. Requests that require national All Voting capacity;
      3. Issues requiring compliance, communications, research/data, or other specialized support;
      4. Significant developments that need to be elevated to organizational leadership.
  2. Track issues
    1. Maintain visibility into significant requests and emerging issues.
    2. For items requiring follow-up: What is the issue, who owns the next step, what is the deadline, has it been resolved?
    3. Surface patterns across states flag when similar issues are emerging in multiple states. What looks isolated in one state may represent a broader pattern requiring national attention or coordination.
  3. Immediately elevate issues that may:
    1. create substantial legal or operational risk;
    2. require rapid communications or organizational response;
    3. represent a significant escalation in election threats or interference;
    4. require resources or decisions beyond the State Director's authority; or have implications beyond the individual state.

How To Apply:

Don’t meet every single requirement? At All Voting, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your experience does not align perfectly with every qualification in this role description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

title: Software Developer
description:
Festina Finance develops modern, high‑performance software used by banks and financial institutions across the Nordics and Europe. Our Advisor platform is a 360° financial advisory solution that helps bank and pension advisors guide customers through credit, mortgage, pension, wealth, and investment decisions.

Advisor is designed to be country‑agnostic and is already live in Denmark, with active expansion into the Nordics, EU, and the UK. We are now looking for a skilled Software Developer to help shape the next generation of the platform.

Why This Role Matters

Financial advisors rely on Advisor to deliver precise, compliant, and trustworthy guidance to their customers. The platform must handle complex financial logic, integrate seamlessly with banking systems, and scale across countries, products, and regulatory environments.

As a developer on the Advisor team, you will:

  • build the financial modelling foundation that powers real advisory conversations
  • ensure that forecasts, key figures, and recommendations are correct and explainable
  • design integrations that connect Advisor to the broader banking ecosystem
  • contribute to a platform used daily by advisors across multiple markets

Your work directly influences how financial decisions are made, from mortgages and pensions to investments and long‑term planning.

About the Role

You will join a cross‑functional team of developers, business analysts, and domain experts working on the core of the Advisor platform. The role combines deep domain logic with solid engineering practices, and you will work across modelling, integrations, data flows, and system behavior.

You will be involved in the full development life cycle: from understanding requirements and refining domain logic to implementing features, improving performance, and ensuring long‑term maintainability.

What You Will Work On

  • Develop and maintain the 360° financial modelling foundation across credit, pensions, wealth, and investments
  • Build and improve integrations with external banking systems and financial APIs
  • Work with complex data models in a layered, multi‑customer, multi‑country architecture
  • Collaborate with analysts, domain experts, and customers to turn requirements into production‑ready code
  • Ensure code quality through testing, documentation, and thorough code review

How We Build Software

  • Java‑based backend with strong domain‑driven design principles
  • Cloud‑native architecture containerized with Docker and orchestrated on Kubernetes
  • Multi‑tenant, layered platform designed for country‑ and customer‑specific extensibility
  • REST APIs with OpenAPI specifications
  • Strong emphasis on automated testing, static analysis, CI/CD, and code quality
  • Increasingly AI‑augmented workflows we invest actively in AI tooling and expect developers to help shape how we use it

What You Bring

You are a developer who enjoys working with domain‑rich systems and solving real business problems through high‑quality engineering.

You have experience with, or a genuine interest in the financial domain, whether that’s banking, credit, pension, insurance, or similar areas.

We welcome applicants at different stages of their career whether you are fresh out of university and ready to learn, or you bring some hands-on experience and want to take the next step.

You’re naturally curious and enjoy learning new domains, technologies, or better ways of solving problems. Collaboration comes easily to you, and you like working closely with developers, analysts, domain experts, and customers. You communicate openly, take initiative, and aren’t afraid to ask questions or challenge assumptions when something doesn’t add up.

Most importantly, you care about the why behind what you build not just the how and you take pride in delivering solutions that are robust, well‑designed, and built to last.

title: Content Specialist III | AI Evaluation & Prompting
description:
We are seeking an experienced Content Specialist III to help evaluate, refine, and improve advanced AI models and products.

In this role, you will work directly with evolving AI systems, testing how they respond across a wide range of topics and conversation types, identifying where they succeed or fall short, and helping shape the prompts, quality standards, and evaluation frameworks that influence how they communicate and behave.

This is a highly hands on opportunity for someone who brings together strong writing and content expertise, curiosity about AI, thoughtful judgment, and a sharp eye for quality. Your work will directly contribute to improving real world AI product experiences and how these systems perform for users.

What You Will Do

• Test new AI model versions across a variety of topics, use cases, and conversation types

• Evaluate model responses against established rubrics, guidelines, and quality standards

• Identify and document specific examples of successful and unsuccessful model behavior

• Write and refine system prompts that help shape model personality, tone, and behavior

• Assess whether evaluation rubrics and quality standards effectively measure model performance

• Perform quality reviews of both human and agent based evaluations to ensure accuracy and compliance

• Conduct hands on experiments with AI models and products

• Investigate model failures and document findings clearly

• Apply detailed instructions and evaluation criteria consistently across a high volume of work

• Adapt quickly as product priorities, model behavior, and evaluation needs evolve

Top Skills

• AI Model Evaluation

• Prompt Writing and Refinement

• Writing and Editing

• Rubric Based Quality Assessment

• Fact Checking and Analytical Judgment

Qualifications

• 5+ years of experience in writing, editing, journalism, production, linguistics, STEM, coding, policy, or another relevant subject matter field

• 1+ year of hands on AI experience preferred, including prompting, annotation, evaluation, or red teaming

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience

• Deep expertise in at least one subject area with the ability to evaluate content as a subject matter expert

• Strong judgment and attention to detail with the ability to consistently apply detailed rubrics, verify information, and identify quality issues

Preferred Experience

• Experience evaluating generative AI or large language model outputs

• Strong fact checking and research skills

• Ability to verify claims against original sources

• Experience conducting detailed failure investigations

• Clear written communication and documentation skills

• Ability to flag questions and blockers early

• Comfortable shifting priorities as product needs change

This team operates in a fast moving environment where priorities can change from day to day. Successful candidates will be comfortable balancing quality, speed, volume, and independent judgment while following detailed instructions.

You should enjoy getting into the details, identifying subtle differences in AI responses, determining why something works or fails, and translating those observations into clear and actionable feedback.

title: Senior Program Analyst
description:
Position Summary

The Senior Program Analyst supporting MSD provides flexible budget and financial management support to both the Budget IAA Team and Budget Execution Team. The Sr. Program Analyst may be assigned across functions as workload demands change, allowing the organization to shift support where needed to address priorities, backlogs, deadlines, and emerging requirements. The Sr. Program Analyst will perform the same general duties, supporting activities related to Interagency Agreements, obligations, de-obligations, spend plan development, budget execution monitoring, unfunded requirements, commitments, expenditures, and unliquidated obligations.

Essential Functions

  • Provide flexible support to both the Budget IAA Team and Budget Execution Team, with assignments shifting across functions based on workload demands, priorities, backlogs, deadlines, and emerging requirements.
  • Support budget and financial management activities related to Interagency Agreements, obligations, de-obligations, spend plan development, budget execution monitoring, unfunded requirements, commitments, expenditures, and unliquidated obligations.
  • Review IAA-related forms and documentation for clarity, completeness, and accuracy of information.
  • Draft, prepare, and review 7600A and 7600B forms.
  • Process Interagency Agreements and assist with resolving issues that may delay approval, obligation, or de-obligation.
  • Officially obligate and de-obligate IAAs on behalf of the organization, as authorized.
  • Monitor obligations to ensure funds are properly obligated in a timely manner.
  • Track and monitor de-obligation requests through completion.
  • Coordinate with internal offices and external partners to resolve IAA documentation, funding, or processing issues.
  • Assist offices in developing and updating budget execution spend plans.
  • Identify and track unfunded requirements.
  • Monitor budget execution against spend plans to identify potential funding surpluses.
  • Support the realignment of available funds to address approved unfunded requirements.
  • Analyze monthly budget expenditures to prepare, compile, and revise budget execution plans.
  • Review budget commitment reports to ensure commitments are properly obligated.
  • Verify that expenditures are posted correctly and identify discrepancies for resolution.
  • Review unliquidated obligation reports to identify items for close-out.
  • Work with program offices to complete the UDO close-out process.
  • Perform other duties as assigned in support of budget and financial management operations.

Job Qualifications

  • Must be a U.S. citizen.
  • Bachelor’s degree (four-year degree) with a major in a related field.
  • A minimum of five years of work experience performing similar business analysis work.
  • Expert-level proficiency in Microsoft Excel, specifically for advanced data analysis, automation, and visualization.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Teams, Word, Outlook, Access and use of multiple monitors.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly in financial contexts.
  • Experience in budget execution, financial analysis, transaction processing, Interagency Agreements, obligations, de-obligations, commitments, expenditures, and unliquidated obligation close-out activities.
  • Experience in developing and maintaining financial reports and data summaries.
  • Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills for financial data analysis.
  • Ability to develop, update, and monitor budget execution spend plans, unfunded requirements, commitment reports, expenditure data, and financial tracking tools.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy in financial reporting.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively.
  • Professional demeanor and adherence to CBP’s standards of conduct.
  • Prior experience with SAP, ServiceNow, and Concur software systems is desired, but not required.
  • Must be able to successfully complete the required U.S. Government background investigation and security clearance process. The selected candidate must be able to obtain and maintain the security clearance required for the position as a condition of employment and continued employment.

OTHER ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

Computer Skills: Proficiency with computers and ability to navigate/enter information into established databases and Microsoft Office products.

Language: Knowledge of the structure and content of the English language including the meaning and spelling of words, rules of composition, and grammar.

Communication: Ability to communicate effectively in writing and in person as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

Customer Service: Ability to address all customer inquiries with a pleasant and patient demeanor.

Math Ability: Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions and decimals. Ability to compute rates, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret information. Ability to choose the right mathematical methods or formulas to solve a problem.

Reasoning Ability: Ability to collect data, define problems, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of instructions dealing with several abstract and concrete variables.

Work Environment: When on site, work is performed in an office cubicle environment with low noise level.

Physical Demands: Employee will have consistent and direct visual contact with multiple computer monitors.

Other Demands:

  • Must comply with all CBP security, training, and onboarding requirements.
  • Professional demeanor and adherence to CBP’s standards of conduct.
  • May be required to work overtime during peak periods and perform mission-essential functions during government furloughs or shutdowns.

This position follows a hybrid work schedule. Due to the onsite requirements of the position, candidates must reside within a 50-mile radius of the designated work location and be able to report onsite as scheduled. The hybrid work schedule is subject to change based on customer and/or business requirements.

title: Catering Service Specialist
description:
Catering Service Specialist – Fine Dining & Events

About the Company

At Tailwind Hospitality, we believe the journey should be just as memorable as the destination. Headquartered in Wilmington, North Carolina, and operating more than 160 locations across 60+ airports and transit stations nationwide, we are a passionate hospitality organization dedicated to creating exceptional guest experiences.

From elevated dining experiences to thoughtfully executed catering events, our teams bring warmth, professionalism, and attention to detail to every guest interaction. We are committed to delivering service that feels personal, polished, and genuinely hospitable.

About the Role

The Catering Service Specialist – Fine Dining & Events plays an integral role in the planning and execution of sophisticated catering experiences. This position is responsible for coordinating events from initial client consultation through final service, ensuring every detail reflects the quality, elegance, and hospitality standards expected of a fine dining experience.

The Catering Service Specialist works closely with clients, culinary leadership, event partners, vendors, and service teams to develop personalized menus, coordinate event logistics, and deliver polished on-site service. The ideal candidate understands that exceptional catering extends beyond the food—it encompasses presentation, timing, service, ambiance, and the overall guest experience.

This role requires a highly organized hospitality professional who can anticipate client needs, manage complex event details, and remain composed and solutions-oriented in a fast-paced environment. The Catering Service Specialist serves as a key ambassador for Tailwind Hospitality and is responsible for ensuring each event is executed with precision, professionalism, and genuine care.

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Proven experience in fine dining, upscale catering, luxury hospitality, event services, or a related hospitality environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver polished, guest-focused service in a high-touch environment.
  • Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, holidays, and extended event hours.
  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.
  • Ability to lift, carry, and transport catering equipment and supplies as required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate or Bachelor’s degree in Hospitality Management, Culinary Arts, Event Management, or a related field.
  • Experience with fine dining restaurants, luxury hotels, private clubs, destination events, or high-end catering.
  • Experience coordinating weddings, corporate events, private dinners, VIP functions, or other elevated hospitality experiences.
  • Experience with event planning, catering, POS, CRM, or inventory management systems.
  • Food safety certification such as ServSafe.
  • Strong knowledge of fine dining service standards, menu presentation, wine and beverage service, and guest etiquette.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple events or complex functions simultaneously.
  • Bilingual or multilingual communication skills.

Responsibilities

  • Consult with clients to understand event objectives, preferences, guest demographics, menu selections, dietary requirements, service expectations, and overall vision.
  • Develop personalized catering experiences in partnership with culinary and hospitality leadership.
  • Coordinate menus, service styles, timelines, staffing requirements, rentals, equipment, décor, and other event details.
  • Collaborate closely with chefs, culinary teams, servers, bartenders, event partners, vendors, and transportation teams to ensure flawless execution.
  • Coordinate the delivery, setup, presentation, service, and breakdown of catered events.
  • Lead or support on-site event operations, ensuring food and beverage service meets established fine dining standards.
  • Ensure proper presentation, timing, portioning, and service of food and beverages throughout the event.
  • Maintain a visible and professional presence during events and serve as the primary point of contact for clients and key stakeholders.
  • Anticipate guest and client needs and proactively address service concerns or unexpected challenges.
  • Resolve operational issues calmly and professionally while protecting the overall guest experience.
  • Ensure compliance with food safety, sanitation, responsible alcohol service, and company standards.
  • Coordinate event transportation and logistics to ensure all food, equipment, rentals, and supplies arrive accurately and on schedule.
  • Conduct event briefings and communicate critical event details to culinary and service teams.
  • Maintain accurate event documentation, client communications, timelines, orders, and inventory records.
  • Assist with post-event follow-up, including client feedback, reconciliation, inventory review, and identification of opportunities to improve future events.
  • Represent Tailwind Hospitality with professionalism, discretion, and a commitment to exceptional hospitality at every event.

Skills & Competencies

Exceptional Hospitality

Demonstrates a genuine passion for hospitality and understands the importance of creating memorable, personalized experiences for every guest.

Fine Dining Service

Understands elevated service standards, including proper table service, food and beverage presentation, service timing, guest etiquette, and attention to detail.

Client Relationship Management

Builds strong relationships with clients and confidently translates their vision and preferences into a professionally executed event.

Organization & Attention to Detail

Effectively manages multiple event components, deadlines, vendors, staffing needs, menus, and logistics while maintaining accuracy and consistency.

Communication

Communicates clearly and professionally with clients, culinary teams, service staff, vendors, and leadership before, during, and after events.

title: Staff Software Engineer- Transaction Platforms Programme (TPP)
description:
GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity.

At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better where we empower our people to master their craft through robust learning and development opportunities all year round.

Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today!

Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg.

A hands-on Staff Software Engineer who will provide technical and technical-product leadership for GovTech's workflow automation platform product, with a particular focus on shaping
and leading a new operational data-layer capability within the platform.

[What you will be working on]

As a Staff Software Engineer in the Transaction Platforms Programme (TPP), you will play a key technical leadership role in shaping and building GovTech’s workflow automation platform product.


The platform product enables government agencies to automate workflows, orchestrate agents, define business rules, and integrate with Whole-of-Government tools. As part of TPP’s broader vision, this platform product works alongside other platform capabilities that agencies can compose to build and deliver digital services.


We are exploring a new capability within this ecosystem to address a key gap: the operational data layer. This is still in its early stages, and you will have the opportunity to shape the solution from the ground up - from understanding the problem and validating product-market fit, to defining its boundaries, architecture, and how it fits cohesively within the platform product and the wider TPP ecosystem.


This is not purely an architecture or delivery role. We are looking for someone who brings strong product thinking alongside deep technical expertise. You will work closely with Product to understand users and the market, evaluate approaches and trade-offs, prototype ideas, and translate these insights into technical product direction.


You will provide technical leadership to the team while remaining hands-on—designing systems, writing and reviewing code, establishing engineering practices, and solving difficult problems around scalability, performance, resilience, and distributed systems.


As we build new capabilities, you will also help us think AI-native from the outset: identifying how agentic and AI capabilities change the way we design the product, its architecture, and the experiences we offer our users.


As a Staff Engineer, your impact will extend beyond a single module or team. You will collaborate with other Staff Engineers, Engineering Managers, Product Managers, and engineers across TPP to ensure that the capabilities we build form a coherent, scalable, and well-architected platform for government.

[What we are looking for]

You should have:

  • Substantial hands-on experience in workflow automation, orchestration, integration platforms, data infrastructure, or closely related product domains. We value experience that gives you a deep understanding of how these systems behave in real-world use, including their constraints, failure modes, and product trade-offs.

  • A strong track record of contributing to product direction, not only technical implementation. You have helped identify what should be built, shaped product capabilities and boundaries, evaluated alternatives, and turned ambiguous problems into solutions that deliver meaningful user value.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills, including experience designing complex systems comprising multiple services and components.

  • Deep understanding of distributed systems and practical experience solving problems involving scalability, performance, resilience, reliability, and failure handling.

  • Strong technical judgement and the ability to reason through unfamiliar or ambiguous problems, identify the important trade-offs, challenge assumptions, and arrive at pragmatic decisions.

  • Experience leading technical direction and execution while remaining hands-on with software development.

  • A track record of raising engineering quality through technical practices, architecture, design and code reviews, mentoring, and improving how teams deliver software.

  • The ability to work effectively across Engineering and Product, connecting user and product needs with technical possibilities and constraints.

  • Experience or strong familiarity with AI-native and agentic systems, and the ability to reason about how these capabilities should influence product and system architecture.

  • Experience building workflow engines, orchestration systems, integration platforms, developer platforms, or operational data infrastructure at scale would be particularly relevant.

What we offer you:

GovTech is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diverse voices and perspectives, as we believe that diversity is the foundation to innovation.

Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks. These include leave benefits to meet your work-life needs and employee wellness programs.

We champion flexible work arrangements (subject to your job role) and trust that you will manage your own time to deliver your best, wherever you are, and whatever works best for you.

Learn more about life inside GovTech at go.gov.sg/GovTechCareers.
Stay connected with us on social media at go.gov.sg/ConnectWithGovTech

title: Director of Fleet Maintenance
description:
Job Title: Director of Fleet Maintenance

Division: Operations

Department: Fleet Maintenance

Work Location: Agency-wide; Nestor Facility (130 Nestor Street) and Myatt Facility (430 Myatt Drive)

Reports to: Deputy Chief Operating Officer, Assets & Infrastructure

Supervises: Senior Fleet Manager (direct); all Fleet Maintenance staff through the management chain

Effective Date: 10/02/2026

Purpose

The Director of Fleet Maintenance is accountable for the performance, direction, and compliance of the agency's fleet maintenance functions: the maintenance, repairs, and availability of all revenue vehicles, non-revenue and support vehicles, and shop equipment across multiple facilities.

The agency is in a state of growth, currently operating nearly 24/7-hour operations and will be 24/7 within the next 1-2 years of this posting. The director establishes the staffing plans, maintenance processes, leadership coverage, shift handoffs, and escalation procedures necessary to support safe and reliable service across all operating periods. This includes ensuring timely response to vehicle failures, clear decision-making authority during overnight and weekend operations, and contingency plans for fleet shortages, severe weather, and other disruptions.

The Director sets strategy, policy, standards, and budget. The Senior Fleet Manager and Fleet Managers carry them out. This position is the department's senior voice to executive leadership, the Federal Transit Administration (FTA), ATU Local 1235, and vehicle manufacturers.

Job Functions

Strategy, Policy and Standards

  • Sets the multi-year direction and annual goals for Fleet Maintenance and aligns them with the agency service plan and capital program.
  • Approves the Fleet Maintenance Plan, department policies, standard operating procedures, and maintenance standards that apply at both facilities.
  • Establishes annual performance targets for the department and each facility with the Senior Fleet Manager and holds the management team accountable for results.
  • Recommends the department organization, position structure, and delegation of authority, and implements approved changes within delegated authority.
  • Ensures maintenance capacity, staffing, equipment, and vehicle availability to support scheduled and planned service expansions, directs recovery plans when fleet availability threatens service delivery.
  • Establishes repair quality assurance standards and directs root cause analysis and corrective action for recurring defects, repeat repairs, and road calls.

Fleet Planning, Specifications and Capital

  • Leads the fleet replacement and expansion plan, including fleet size, mix, propulsion technology, and replacement timing against FTA useful life benchmarks.
  • Develops vehicle specifications for all revenue and non-revenue rolling stock and works with manufacturers on engineering design to improve reliability, safety, and customer experience.
  • Exercises vehicle acceptance authority as delegated by the agency, on the commissioning findings presented by the Senior Fleet Manager.
  • Prioritizes and submits the department's capital requests for shop equipment, bays, fueling, washing, and supporting infrastructure in coordination with other Maintenance leadership.
  • Recommends vehicle disposition and changes to the contingency fleet, implements approved actions within delegated authority, and coordinated required approvals with Grants department and agency leadership.

Budget and Financial Control

  • Develops, defends, and is accountable for the department's operating and capital budgets.
  • Approves expenditures within delegated authority and reviews cost/benefit analysis for major decisions, including rebuild-versus-replace and in-house-versus-vendor
  • Reports maintenance cost per revenue mile and budget variances to the Deputy COO and senior leadership
  • Oversees maintenance contracts and vendor performance with Procurement and Materials Management.
  • Ensures department purchases comply with agency procurement policies, purchasing thresholds, delegated authority, and required solicitation procedures, coordinates planned purchases and contract changes with procurement.
  • Oversees warranty recovery, manufacturer campaigns and recalls, and verification that contracted repairs meet agency standards.

Regulatory Compliance and State of Good Repair

  • Is accountable for compliance with federal, state, and local safety, maintenance, and environmental requirements that apply to fleet maintenance.
  • Is accountable for the agency fleet spare ratio and for the accuracy of fleet data reported to the FTA and the National Transit Database.
  • Provides rolling stock and equipment condition data, targets, and investment priorities to the agency Transit Asset Management (TAM) program under 49 CFR Part 625.
  • Leads the department's preparation for and response to FTA Triennial Reviews, state inspections, and internal audits, and approves corrective actions.
  • Sponsors the department safety program and ensures corrective actions from accidents, injuries, and reported hazards are closed.
  • Ensure vehicles with safety-critical defects are withheld from service and establishes documented return-to-service authorization standards in coordination with Safety and Operations.

Labor Relations and Workforce

  • Represents company leadership as a delegate for second step discipline and grievance matters and ensures the collective bargaining agreement is applied the same way across facilities.
  • Develops the department staffing plan and recommends new positions during Fiscal Year budget review periods
  • Sponsors the mechanic career ladder, the apprentice program, and succession planning for supervisory and management positions.
  • Ensures role-specific technical training, demonstrated competency, and qualification tracking for maintenance personnel in coordination with Training; identifies and addresses skill gaps.

title: Computer Vision Engineer
description:
ABOUT REVEL

REVEL is an AI robotics company developing physical intelligence for general-purpose humanoid robots. We capture the force, dexterity, and intent of human work with our Neural Gambit wearable, and use it to train RAI, the intelligence that powers our robots. REVEL is headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with R&D and engineering facilities in Prague and Hradec Králové, Czech Republic. This role is on-site in our Prague lab.

THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced computer vision engineer to build the perception that lets our humanoid robot, GENESIS, see and understand its workspace in real time. You will turn REVEL's recordings of skilled human work, captured with several cameras and the Neural Gambit wearable, into models that track hands, tools, and objects in 3D. Then you will get those models running on the robot.

Every manipulation skill the robot learns depends on seeing hands, tools, and objects accurately. Perception errors show up as failed grasps on a customer's floor.

You will join a small Perception team in Prague and work closely with our Robot Learning and Data Collection teams. Most of the team is early in their careers, so you will help set how we build, evaluate, and ship models, and support the junior engineers along the way.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Build hand, tool and object tracking in 3D from our multi-camera and wearable recordings of people doing manual work.

  • Develop detection, segmentation, pose estimation and 3D scene understanding for the robot's manipulation skills.

  • Calibrate and synchronise multi-camera and depth setups in the lab and on the robot, and keep them accurate over time.

  • Build training and evaluation pipelines that anyone on the team can rerun months later: data, labelling, dataset versioning and experiment tracking.

  • Design evaluations around what the robot needs, not only benchmark scores, and find out why a model fails on real data.

  • Get models running in real time on the robot's onboard GPU (ONNX, TensorRT, quantisation or similar).

  • Work with Robot Learning and Data Collection on what to record and what perception the next skill needs.

  • Help set engineering standards in a small, young team.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 3+ years of hands-on computer vision work in industry or research, with models you trained yourself running on real camera data, not only on benchmarks.

  • Strong Python and PyTorch.

  • Solid Linear Algebra and 3D Computer Vision fundamentals.

  • Deep-learning fundamentals for vision (detection, segmentation, pose estimation or 3D vision) and rigorous evaluation.

  • Experience with real cameras and real-world data: calibration, multi-camera setups, noise, lighting and latency.

  • Experience taking a model from training to real-time inference on a robot or an edge device.

  • Good engineering practice: Git, Linux, clean code and reproducible experiments.

  • Honesty about what you know. You say "I don't know" when you don't, take criticism of your ideas well, and still defend a good idea with evidence.

  • Fluent English for daily work with colleagues in Prague, Hradec Králové and the US.

  • Able to work full-time on-site at our Prague lab.

BONUS POINTS, BUT NOT ESSENTIAL

  • Hand and body pose tracking, or egocentric video.

  • Depth sensors, point clouds or 3D reconstruction.

  • Experience with IMU and sensor fusion.

  • Visual SLAM, VGGT and any other modern NN-based methods in computer vision.

  • Hands-on hardware: you have integrated sensors on a real robot or product prototype.

  • Image processing pipeline: from raw sensor data to .jpg.

  • ROS 2.

  • OpenCV, numpy, scipy, pandas/Polars.

  • Vision-language-action or foundation models.

  • Publications in computer vision, ML or robotics.

WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT

  • This is not a research-only role. Success means models that work on the robot, and getting them there is part of your job.

  • This is not a benchmark role. You will work with real cameras, real lighting and messy recordings every day.

  • This is not a junior or internship position. We are looking for someone who can own a perception problem from the data to the robot.

WHAT YOU'LL GET OUT OF IT

  • The chance to build the eyes of a humanoid robot, trained on REVEL's own recordings of skilled human work.

  • Data most computer vision engineers never get: multi-camera recordings of real manual work, together with what the Neural Gambit wearable captures.

  • Your models run on robots in the same lab where you work.

  • Real ownership of the perception stack, and room to take on broader responsibility as the team grows.

WHY REVEL

  • The Team: Colleagues from NVIDIA, SpaceX and Neura Robotics, in a small team with short paths to decisions.

  • Real Technology: You see the robots in the lab every day, not just in a pitch deck.

  • A Fast-Growing US Startup: Founded in 2025 and building its team in the Czech Republic.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Competitive compensation based on experience.

  • Unlimited Paid Time Off: Real flexibility to take time away when you need it. We trust our people to own their work, their time and their results.

  • Lunch, On Us: Complimentary lunch every working day, plus coffee, snacks and drinks whenever you need a boost.

  • Prague, On-Site: Our office is at U Pekáren 1645/1, Prague, Hostivař.

HOW TO APPLY

Apply through the link on this posting. Along with your CV, you will fill in a short form.

title: Associate, In-Process QA, MG/PG
description:
Job Description

Date

06/2025

Location

1300 Airport Road, North Brunswick NJ 08902

Title

Associate, In-Process Quality Assurance MFG/PKG

Department

Quality Assurance Operation Support

Reports to

Quality Assurance Manager/ VP of QA

FLSA (Exempt or Non-Exempt

Non-Exempt

Role Overview

The IPQA performs line inspection as part of the cGMP, SOPs, and policy compliance requirements as per CFR part 111. Performs In-process quality testing in manufacturing and/or packaging areas according to prescribed timelines and accurately captures test results in batch records. The Inspector performs calibrations & measurements on raw materials, bulk products, finished products and packaging components as required in batch records and SOP’s. This position reports to the QA Manager and is a key member of the Quality Assurance group. The IPQA Associate is a highly organized self-starter who can work independently, demonstrates a positive attitude, and a bias for action.

Areas of Responsibility

IPQA – Level 1: To support In-process quality assurance activities by performing routine checks and verifications during manufacturing and/or packaging of nutraceutical products. This role ensures that all processes comply with applicable GMP, SOPs, and regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities:

🔹 Manufacturing Support

  • Perform line clearance before starting blending, granulation, compression, encapsulation, coating processes.
  • Perform In-process checks:
    • Blend uniformity sampling
    • Tablet/capsule weight variation
    • Hardness, friability, and disintegration tests etc as applicable
  • Verify equipment cleaning and area hygiene as per SOP.
  • Collect and label In-process and stability samples under supervision.

🔹 Packaging Support

  • Ensure line clearance before packaging activities.
  • Perform In-process checks:
    • Batch number and expiry date printing
    • Label application and carton sealing
    • Primary and secondary packaging integrity etc as applicable
  • Assist in reconciliation of packaging materials (e.g., printed cartons, leaflets, labels).

🔹 Documentation

  • Record observations in IPQA checklists, logbooks, and batch records.
  • Maintain GMP documentation in real-time (legible and error-free).
  • Escalate any deviation or abnormality immediately to the QA Executive/Supervisor.

🔹 Compliance & Safety

  • Adhere to company GMP, SOP, and Hygiene policies.
  • Use PPE appropriately.
  • Support during internal/external audits by providing necessary records.
  • Cleans up work following the completion of a shift.
  • Meets all safety expectations and follows all safety practices.
  • Works extended hours and occasional weekend overtime.
  • Other duties as assigned
  • Other Responsibilities Including Safety:


IPQA – Level 2: To independently perform and document In-process quality assurance activities at all critical stages of manufacturing and packaging of nutraceutical products, ensuring compliance with GMP, SOPs, and regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities:

🔹 Manufacturing Stage (Granulation, Blending, Compression, Encapsulation, Coating )

  • Carry out and document line clearance activities before starting each manufacturing batch.
  • Conduct in-process checks independently:
    • Blend uniformity sampling
    • Tablet/capsule weight variation
    • Hardness, friability, thickness, and disintegration
    • In-process controls as per BMR specifications
  • Verify equipment cleanliness status, calibration, and logbook entries.
  • Monitor and record environmental conditions in production areas (temperature, RH, differential pressure).

🔹 Packaging Stage

  • Conduct line clearance for primary and secondary packaging (bottles, strips, blister, cartons).
  • Perform and document:
    • Batch coding verification (batch no., Mfg/Exp date)
    • Packaging material correctness (labels, leaflets, cartons)
    • Sealing integrity checks (blisters, induction seals)
    • Online rejection bin and reconciliation checks
  • Ensure correct usage of approved packaging materials with status labels.

🔹 Documentation & Compliance

  • Fill Batch Manufacturing Records (BMR) and Batch Packaging Records (BPR) in real-time.
  • Record IPQA observations and results as per SOPs ( legible and error free).
  • Initiate and report deviations, OOS/OOT, and non-conformities to QA Supervisor/ Manager.
  • Support CAPA implementation and change controls.

🔹 General QA Duties

  • Ensure compliance with GMP, GLP, and data integrity principles.
